:PROPERTIES:

Converts [[file:glossary.org::#term/cardinality][cardinality]] into the number of [[file:glossary.org::#term/advisory-lock][advisory-lock]] permits: ~:singleton~ allows one instance, ~:pool~ allows N, and ~:per-pod~ runs independently on each process. These permits are concurrency controls, not graph [[file:glossary.org::#term/slot][argument slots]].

* 4. reconcile-once!
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: services/reconcile-once!
:FILE: src/graphden/services/reconciler.clj
:LINE: 392
:MINS: 3.6

Performs one [[file:glossary.org::#term/reconciliation][reconciliation]] pass: reads desired services, detects configuration changes, plans starts/stops, and attempts to acquire [[file:glossary.org::#term/cardinality][execution permits]]. Both write notifications and periodic ticks invoke it, so later passes can recover after missed notifications or a crashed instance owner.

Reads endpoint metadata from the service handle and adds the starting executor's reachable host. The resulting host and port are recorded on the service-instance row, whose [[file:glossary.org::#term/fleet][heartbeat]] is refreshed during [[file:glossary.org::#term/reconciliation][reconciliation]]. Other services resolve this row to find an active endpoint.

:LINE: 119
:MINS: 2.3

Checks service handles for liveness and exit status. A stopped instance loses its stored row and [[file:glossary.org::#term/cardinality][execution permit]]; restart policy then determines whether to restart any exit, only a failure, or neither. Active instances refresh their [[file:glossary.org::#term/fleet][heartbeats]].

Resolves a service identity to an active endpoint on the caller's branch, preferring a live local instance, then a finite HTTP publication and an addon resolver; otherwise it reports ~:service/not-running~. The ~:fn-ref~ argument passes identity without executing the named function.

* 10. publish!
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: services/publish!
:FILE: src/graphden/http_host/core.clj
:LINE: 199
:MINS: 3.4
:END:

Authorizes a typed request handler on an exact branch without invoking it. The existing graph writer and branch guards precede the publication capacity lock; the session lease and optional isolated app route commit together. The client supplies a create-only UUID so lost-response cleanup can revoke the exact publication.

Serializes finite publication admission and cleanup across all pods using a short PostgreSQL advisory transaction lock. Callbacks must not acquire graph or branch locks; this preserves graph → branch → capacity lock ordering during branch deletion.

Declares a PostgreSQL-backed job queue with status, attempts, due time, and a visibility lock. Claiming uses ~FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED~; notifications wake waiting consumers. The consumer loop is composed in graph definitions, while database operations remain small primitives.

* 15. placement-for
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: services/placement-for
:FILE: src/graphden/fleet/placement.clj
:LINE: 11
:MINS: 1.1
:END:

Finds the placement of an [[file:glossary.org::#term/fleet][execution cell]], identified by organisation and entry-function ID. Placement records identify the responsible executor; the highest [[file:glossary.org::#term/invalidation][epoch]] wins when records differ. Routing and relocation use this shared placement information.

Combines a [[file:glossary.org::#term/fleet][cell]]'s dependency-graph size and current organisation load into a numeric weight. Placement algorithms use this estimate to compare [[file:glossary.org::#term/fleet][cells]]; it is a scheduling estimate, not a measurement of every function's execution cost.

* 18. pack
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: services/pack
:FILE: src/graphden/fleet/packer.clj
:LINE: 69
:MINS: 2.7
:END:

Builds a placement by sorting [[file:glossary.org::#term/fleet][cells]] from heaviest to lightest and assigning each to the currently least-loaded executor. This greedy longest-processing-time-first strategy is an approximation for balancing load, not an exhaustive search for an optimal arrangement.

- source :: [[file:../../../src/graphden/fleet/packer.clj::(defn pack][src/graphden/fleet/packer.clj:69]]

* 19. rebalance
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: services/rebalance
:FILE: src/graphden/fleet/rebalance.clj
:LINE: 81
:MINS: 5.0
:END:

Improves an existing placement one move at a time, moving a [[file:glossary.org::#term/fleet][cell]] from a busier executor when that reduces load spread sufficiently. ~:min-improvement~ prevents moves for negligible gains. This heuristic limits unnecessary moves but does not prove a globally minimum move count.

- source :: [[file:../../../src/graphden/fleet/rebalance.clj::(defn rebalance][src/graphden/fleet/rebalance.clj:81]]

:PROPERTIES:

Plans one control tick without performing moves. Unassigned [[file:glossary.org::#term/fleet][cells]] receive initial placements immediately; rebalancing waits for imbalance to persist for ~:sustain-ticks~. This delay avoids reacting to brief load spikes.
